stem: A provider orders cystatin C with eGFR for a client whose very low muscle mass may make creatinine-based estimates less reliable. Why is cystatin C useful in this situation?

options.A: Cystatin C provides another index of glomerular filtration and is less dependent on skeletal muscle mass than creatinine, making it useful when creatinine may mislead.
options.B: Cystatin C primarily measures hepatic synthetic function, so it is used to estimate liver reserve when creatinine cannot be interpreted reliably.
options.C: Cystatin C is most useful when skeletal muscle mass is typical because abnormal muscle mass produces the same limitation seen with serum creatinine.
options.D: Cystatin C is unrelated to glomerular filtration and is ordered mainly to evaluate electrolyte balance rather than kidney filtration.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories guidance describes cystatin C as an index of GFR that is especially useful when serum creatinine may be misleading, including in malnourished patients or those with abnormally high or low muscle mass. Unlike creatinine, cystatin C is not produced solely by skeletal muscle and its serum concentration is less affected by muscle mass. Therefore A is correct. B assigns the test to liver function, C reverses its main advantage in this scenario, and D incorrectly denies its direct relationship to GFR.
educational_objective: Explain why cystatin C can improve GFR assessment when creatinine-based estimates are confounded by atypical skeletal muscle mass.
source_document_title: Cystatin C with Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR), Serum (CSTCE)

source_locator: Useful For: index of GFR especially where serum creatinine may be misleading, including malnourished patients. Clinical Information: cystatin C is freely filtered; serum concentration is inversely related to GFR and not greatly affected by body mass; cystatin C eGFR may have advantages with abnormally high or low muscle mass. Mayo Insights: cystatin C is not linked to skeletal muscle mass like creatinine.
source_claim_supported: Cystatin C is a GFR marker less tied to skeletal muscle mass than creatinine and is useful when atypical muscle mass makes creatinine-based estimates less reliable.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor and interpret diagnostic/laboratory findings and recognize limitations of testing.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only 'only' wording and balanced all alternatives as parallel explanations of the test's role.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — current Mayo evidence directly supports cystatin C for GFR estimation when creatinine is confounded by abnormal muscle mass; A uniquely matches.
